source.title: Open problems on graphs arising from geometric topology

accepted.question_text: Let K be a tree embedded in the Euclidean plane R^2 and let epsilon be positive. Say that K is genuinely epsilon-disjoinable if there is a continuous or piecewise-linear map f: K -> R^2 such that K and f(K) are disjoint and every point x of K moves by less than epsilon, |x - f(x)| < epsilon. Say that K is epsilon-spanned if two closed round disks of diameter epsilon, whose centers move continuously on K and are never allowed to intersect, cannot be moved so that their two traces on K become the same. Say that K is symmetrically epsilon-spanned if such disks cannot exchange their positions. Does genuine epsilon-disjoinability imply epsilon-spannedness, and does symmetric epsilon-spannedness imply epsilon-spannedness for plane trees?

Let K be a tree embedded in R^2 and let epsilon be positive. An epsilon-triod is a plane triod made from three arcs meeting only at one common point, with each arm containing a point whose distance from the union of the other two arms is greater than epsilon. A tree is epsilon-narrow if some arc I contained in K has every point of K within distance epsilon of I. A tree is epsilon-spanned if two non-intersecting closed disks of diameter epsilon with centers constrained to move on K cannot move so that their traces on K are the same. Prove or disprove the two narrowness assertions: every plane tree with no epsilon-triods is 10 epsilon-narrow, and every epsilon-spanned plane tree is 10 epsilon-narrow.

Let K be a plane tree in R^2 with diameter 1 and let epsilon be positive. A tree is epsilon-chainable if it is the union of closed sets C_1,...,C_n, each of diameter less than epsilon, such that C_i intersects only its immediate neighbors C_{i-1} and C_{i+1}. A tree is epsilon-spanned if two non-intersecting round disks of diameter epsilon with centers moving on K cannot move so that their traces on K are the same. Is every epsilon-spanned plane tree of diameter 1 necessarily 10 epsilon-chainable?

For finite graphs K, find structural descriptions of when K is basically embeddable into each of the product spaces R x S, T_3 x S, S x S, and X x Y where X and Y are graphs. Here S denotes the circle graph used in the obstruction list, T_3 denotes the 3-od graph used in products of stars, and a basic embedding into X x Y is the product-space analogue of a basic embedding into R^2: every continuous real-valued function on the embedded copy of K should decompose as the sum of one continuous function depending only on the X-coordinate and one depending only on the Y-coordinate.

Given any triple of finite graphs K, X, and Y, is there an algorithm that decides whether K is basically embeddable in the product X x Y? In this setting, basic embeddability means that K embeds into X x Y in such a way that each continuous real-valued function on K can be written as a sum of a continuous function of the X-coordinate and a continuous function of the Y-coordinate.

For every fixed pair of finite graphs X and Y, prove or disprove that there are only finitely many prohibited subgraphs whose absence characterizes finite graphs K that are basically embeddable in X x Y. Basic embeddability is the product-space version of decomposing every continuous real-valued function on K as a sum of functions of the two coordinates.

Let f: K -> R^2 be a piecewise-linear map from a graph K to the plane. Say that f is approximable by embeddings if for every epsilon > 0 there is an embedding of K into R^2 that is epsilon-close to f. The van Kampen obstruction theta(f) is obtained by perturbing f to general position and algebraically counting intersections between images of disjoint oriented edges of K. A necessary condition for approximability by embeddings is theta(f) = 0. Prove the converse, theta(f) = 0 implies f is approximable by embeddings, in each of these cases: K is arbitrary and f is monotone; K is an arc; or K is a tree.

Find algebraic graph-theoretic characterizations of colored graphs that represent closed piecewise-linear 4-manifolds whose fundamental groups lie in specified classes such as finite groups, free products, surface groups, poly-(finite or cyclic) groups, or amenable groups. A colored graph represents a closed PL n-manifold when its associated colored-graph polyhedron is PL homeomorphic to that manifold.

Find algebraic graph-theoretic characterizations of colored graphs that represent fibered families of PL manifolds, including good torus fibrations, surface bundles, Seifert manifolds, manifolds with torus actions, and circle bundles. The colored graph should represent the manifold through the standard construction associating an n-dimensional polyhedron to an (n+1)-colored regular graph.
Find an algebraic characterization of colored graphs whose associated colored-graph polyhedron is PL homeomorphic to the standard n-sphere S^n for n >= 3.

Construct a simple algorithm that takes an oriented link in the oriented 3-sphere S^3 together with surgery coefficients and outputs a colored graph representing the closed 3-manifold obtained by performing that surgery.
Given a colored graph representing a closed PL n-manifold M, derive purely combinatorial descriptions of the higher homotopy groups pi_i(M) for all i >= 2.
Find combinatorial conditions on a colored graph representing a PL manifold M that imply specified homotopy groups of M vanish, especially conditions forcing pi_1(M) or pi_2(M) to be trivial.
Find combinatorial conditions that recognize when a colored graph represents a homology n-sphere for n >= 3.

Let M and M' be closed orientable PL 4-manifolds. For a closed PL n-manifold, define its k-complexity c_k(M) by minimizing, over all colored graphs representing M, the rank of the chain module C_{n-k}(G), and define the reduced complexity by subtracting the corresponding baseline complexity of the n-sphere. Is the reduced 4-complexity additive under connected sum, namely does c_tilde_4(M # M') = c_tilde_4(M) + c_tilde_4(M') hold?

For a closed PL n-manifold M, call a colored graph G representing M minimal when it realizes the n-complexity c_n(M), meaning that the rank invariant beta_n(G) used in the complexity definition equals c_n(M). Study the graph-theoretic properties of such minimal colored graphs and find combinatorial characterizations of them.

Closed 3-manifolds of Heegaard genus two can be represented by 4-colored graphs constructed from six positive integers arranged as (n_1, h_1; n_2, h_2; n_3, h_3). Determine the relations between two such 6-tuples that make their colored graphs represent the same 3-manifold, and classify the homeomorphism types of Heegaard genus two 3-manifolds in terms of these representing 6-tuples.

For the 4-colored graph construction of closed Heegaard genus two 3-manifolds from 6-tuples (n_1, h_1; n_2, h_2; n_3, h_3), find arithmetic conditions on the six integers that are exactly those yielding homology 3-spheres.

For a Heegaard genus two 3-manifold represented by a colored graph arising from a 6-tuple of integers (n_1, h_1; n_2, h_2; n_3, h_3), write a finite presentation of its fundamental group directly in terms of that 6-tuple.

needs_review.question_text_raw: Problem 3.10 asks to prove a conjecture about connected compacta basically embeddable in R^2, but the exact conjectural description is referred to from another work rather than fully stated in the readable source text.

Problem 4.8 asks for analogous descriptions of H_1 and H^1 of the deleted product of a graph, including generators and dimensions, but the OCR corrupts several homology symbols and generator formulas.
Conjecture 5.15 concerns the complexity of simply-connected closed PL 4-manifolds, but the OCR corrupts the displayed equality involving c_2(M), c_4(M), and the Euler characteristic.
Conjecture 5.17 states an inequality for triangulations of closed PL 2k-manifolds with equality characterized by neighborliness, but the OCR omits the displayed inequality.
Problem 5.18 asks for the relationship between two preceding concepts, but one of those concepts depends on the missing inequality in Conjecture 5.17.

trace.notes: Normalized the single input as a zbMATH resolver URL with identifier 1308017. Local shell networking could not resolve zbmath.org or api.zbmath.org, so local shard metadata and browser search were used for bounded recovery.

Resolver metadata in local shard files identified the exact work title and DOI 10.1016/S0166-8641(97)00093-X. Search confirmed the same title at ScienceDirect, Unimore, ResearchGate, and Academia. ScienceDirect and Unimore exposed metadata or abstracts, while the Academia page exposed readable OCR text for the same article and was selected as the primary HTML source.

Mapped the readable HTML/OCR source into sections: Introduction; Section 2 on generalizations of Moore's theorem; Section 3 on basic embedding; Section 4 on approximability of maps by embeddings; Section 5 on PL manifolds and colored graphs. Likely open-problem regions are explicitly labelled Problem or Conjecture in Sections 2 through 5.
Extracted Problems 2.5, 2.7, and 2.9 from the section on plane-tree analogues of Moore-type continua questions.

Extracted Problems 3.10, 3.13, 3.14, and 3.15 from the basic-embedding section. Problem 3.10 was held for review because the underlying conjectural description is not stated completely in the source text.
Extracted Problems 4.5 and 4.8 from the approximability section. Problem 4.8 was held for review because OCR corruption prevents reliable reconstruction of the homology formulas.

Extracted Problems 5.4, 5.5, 5.6, 5.7, 5.9, 5.10, 5.12, 5.16, 5.18, 5.20, 5.21, and 5.22, plus Conjectures 5.14, 5.15, and 5.17. Conjectures 5.15 and 5.17 and Problem 5.18 were held for review because key formulas or references are missing after OCR.

Rephrased the fibered-manifold characterization problem while keeping only the listed manifold families recoverable from OCR.
Restated the standard-sphere recognition problem for colored graphs.
Expanded the surgery input as an oriented link with coefficients in S^3 and the requested output as a representing colored graph.
Restated the problem of deriving higher homotopy groups from colored graph data.
Restated the homotopy-vanishing criteria problem and kept the examples pi_1 and pi_2.
Restated the homology-sphere recognition problem for n at least 3.
Expanded reduced complexity from the preceding definitions and stated Conjecture 5.14 as additivity under connected sum.
Expanded minimal colored graph terminology from the local definition preceding the problem.
Expanded the 6-tuple construction using Theorem 5.19 and kept the two requested tasks: tuple relations and homeomorphism classification.

Restated the finite-presentation problem for fundamental groups in terms of the 6-tuple.
